solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Unnamed pet fed by book group (8)

indicators.note: 'un-named' read literally means stripped of its N, the standard abbreviation for name
something fed takes food inside it, so the pet word takes the B into its middle

blocks.note: canoodle = to pet, cuddle; drop N (name)
B is the abbreviation for book

annotation.surface: A nameless pet is being fed by a group reading a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is the verb here: to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle. It hides behind the picture of an animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Caboodle survives almost only in the idiom 'the whole caboodle', meaning the whole lot or group.

entries.clue: Half-capsized vessels tip (4)

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, and 'half' limits that to one half of the word, the back half here

blocks.note: cups are drinking vessels; its second half PS turns to SP

annotation.surface: Boats have half-capsized and are tipping over.
annotation.walkthrough: The vessels look like boats but are cups, which is what makes 'capsized' so natural.
annotation.definitionFit: A cusp is the pointed end where two curves meet, as on a tooth or the horns of a crescent moon.

entries.clue: Total enthusiast supporting British game and veg (9,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever supports another word sits beneath it, holding it up

blocks.note: utter = total, as in utter nonsense
a nut = a fan, as in golf nut

annotation.surface: A total fan of a British sport who also likes vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Total enthusiast' reads as one phrase and is one, an utter nut, placed below the British.
annotation.definitionFit: Butternut squash is a pear-shaped orange-fleshed squash, a specific example of veg.

entries.clue: Fine house under protection of Buddhist state (8)

indicators.note: something under another's protection is sheltered within it, so the house sits inside the Buddhist

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
HO is the abbreviation for house

annotation.surface: A fine house enjoys the protection of a Buddhist state such as Tibet or Bhutan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buddhist state' reads as one idea, but the state is the definition on its own and the Buddhist is a lama.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Oklahoma is one of the fifty states of the USA.

entries.clue: Beaten sailor conceding nothing retreats (5)

indicators.note: something beaten, like metal or eggs, is knocked out of its original form, so the letters change shape
to concede is to give something up, so the sailor gives up its O

blocks.note: O = nothing, zero; it is removed, leaving SAILR

annotation.surface: A defeated sailor gives up without a point and falls back.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a match report, and 'retreats' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den, a place it retreats to, so lairs are retreats in the sense of hideaways.

entries.clue: Agency’s order returned work in pieces (6)

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the CIA's, the US intelligence agency
OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

annotation.surface: An agency sends back an order for a job that arrived in bits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work in pieces' sounds like a botched job but describes the artwork exactly.
annotation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a work of art built from small pieces of tile or glass, so the definition is a cryptic description.

entries.clue: Annoyed after raising available yield (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a part lifts it to the top, so the phrase is read after that part has been moved up

blocks.note: out = available, as a book newly out
annoyed = PUT OUT; its OUT is lifted above PUT

annotation.surface: Someone annoyed at having to raise the available yield.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue names the part to move: of PUT OUT, the 'available' part is the one raised to the top of the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Output and yield are plain synonyms for the amount something produces, as in a farm's or factory's yield.

entries.clue: Line-up at ten excited couple third from the end (15)

indicators.note: excited particles or people move about wildly, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: anagram of LINEUP AT TEN, 11 letters
to mate = to couple, pair up

annotation.surface: A line-up of people excitedly pairs off at ten o'clock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple' is a verb placed after the anagram, not part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin ante (before) and paenultimus (almost last): the one before the penultimate, third from the end.

entries.clue: Chip in centre of tabula: sorry about that (10)

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, here the two middle letters of a six-letter word
about in the sense of around, so the sorry word surrounds the centre

blocks.note: the middle two letters of TABULA

annotation.surface: Someone apologises for putting a chip in the middle of a tablet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sorry about that' reads as an apology tacked on at the end; 'about' is doing the work of a container.
annotation.definitionFit: To chip in is an informal idiom for putting money or effort into a shared pot.

entries.clue: Rejection of the other new American bicycle (8)

indicators.note: a new version of something has been remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

annotation.surface: Someone turns down a new American bike for the other one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British slang for sex, so rejecting it is celibacy.
annotation.definitionFit: Celibacy is abstaining from sex, which coy British slang calls 'a bit of the other'.

entries.clue: Object launched from rocky islet late (9)

indicators.note: rocky also means unsteady, and letters on unsteady ground wobble into a new order

annotation.surface: Something launched late from a rocky little island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocky islet' reads as scenery, but 'rocky' is what shakes the letters up.
annotation.definitionFit: An artificial satellite is sent up by rocket, so an object launched describes it well.

entries.clue: Huge giants essentially tracking bird (5)

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is at its heart, so take the middle letters
to track something is to follow its trail, so this part comes behind the bird

blocks.note: a tit is a small bird
the middle two letters of GIANTS

annotation.surface: Huge giants follow the trail of a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge' is an adjective, and titan works as one: a titan struggle, a titan effort.
annotation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, so titan used as an adjective means huge.

entries.clue: Coach abandoning first-class college (4)

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so the coach word leaves its A out

annotation.surface: A coach walks out on a top college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer or a bus; it is the verb, teach.
annotation.definitionFit: Tech is the British short form for a technical college, where vocational subjects are taught.

entries.clue: Omit scrubbing soft garment one takes off (3,6)

indicators.note: to scrub a plan is to cancel it, so the soft letter is cancelled from the word

blocks.note: p = piano, soft in music; scrubbed from SKIP
a jumper is a British word for a sweater

annotation.surface: Skip washing the soft jumper someone takes off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' suggests removing a garment, which the jumper encourages; the ski jumper takes off from the ramp.
annotation.definitionFit: A ski jumper launches from the end of a ramp, so 'one takes off' is a cryptic description of the flight.

entries.clue: Ignoring borders, wimpy pilots over time defect (10)

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, and ignoring them drops both
in a down clue, one thing over another sits above it, so the pilots come before the time

annotation.surface: Weedy pilots cross the border and defect over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Defect' looks like the verb to change sides, a natural fit with 'borders'; here it is the noun, a flaw.
annotation.definitionFit: Defect as a noun means a flaw, and an impairment is a flaw in how something works, such as a hearing impairment.

entries.clue: Obsessive national hiding number in coat (10)

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the national holds the number within
placed in, so the whole assembly goes inside the coat

annotation.surface: An obsessive foreigner hides a number inside his coat.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a nest of two containers, so the smallest one is built first and the coat wraps it last.
annotation.definitionFit: A monomaniac is fixated on a single subject, so obsessive works as a noun: an obsessive person.

entries.clue: Iris scan arranged for poet’s host? (8)

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in order, as with flowers, so the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Irises and other flowers arranged for a poet's host.
annotation.walkthrough: Wordsworth saw 'a host, of golden daffodils', and daffodils are narcissi; the question mark flags that allusion.
annotation.definitionFit: Daffodils belong to the genus Narcissus, so Wordsworth's host of golden daffodils was a host of narcissi.

entries.clue: Slight man finally saved by vessel (4)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of the word
someone saved by a boat is taken aboard, so the letter goes inside the vessel

annotation.surface: A slightly built man is finally rescued by a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective, thin; it is the noun, an insult.
annotation.definitionFit: A slight is a noun for an insult by neglect, and a snub is exactly that, a deliberate cold shoulder.

entries.clue: African petition blocked by Europeans (8)

indicators.note: a pipe blocked by something has it lodged inside, so the Europeans sit inside the petition

annotation.surface: An African's petition is blocked by European officials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Europeans' tempts a solver to write E for European; here it is a whole nation, the Danes.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: a Sudanese person, from Sudan, is one kind of African.

entries.clue: Portion of oatcakes rolled in minutes (4)

indicators.note: a portion is a piece of the whole, so the answer is a piece of the word
something rolled over ends up the other way round, so the piece reads backwards

annotation.surface: A piece of oatcake is rolled in a coating for a few minutes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' looks like time; it is the written record of a meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: Acta is the Latin word used for official records of proceedings, the same sense as a meeting's minutes.

entries.clue: Swimmer welcome around Yankee isle (4,6)

indicators.note: around in the sense of surrounding, so the welcome word wraps the other letters

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
Mull is an island off the west coast of Scotland

annotation.surface: An American swimmer is welcomed on arrival at an island.
annotation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish, not a person, and Yankee is only a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a cryptic hint by example: the grey mullet is a coastal fish, and fish are swimmers.

entries.clue: End up consuming second small Manhattan cocktail (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom upwards, which reverses the word
to consume is to take something in, so the reversed word takes the others inside it

blocks.note: an end = an aim, goal; turned up gives MIA
a mo = a moment, a second

annotation.surface: Someone finishes a small drink in Manhattan.
annotation.walkthrough: A Manhattan is itself a cocktail, which tempts; here Manhattan just means American.
annotation.definitionFit: Mimosa is the American name for champagne with orange juice, which Britain calls a Buck's Fizz, hence a Manhattan cocktail.

entries.clue: Mass shortened to accommodate model is essential (9)

indicators.note: a shortened word is cut down at the end, so the Mass loses its last letter
to accommodate a guest is to make room inside, so the model goes within the Mass

blocks.note: REQUIEM, a Mass for the dead, less M
to sit = to model for an artist

annotation.surface: A church service is cut short to make room for a model, and that is essential.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mass is a specific one, the Requiem, and the model is a verb, what a person does for a painter.
annotation.definitionFit: Requisite, from Latin requirere, is a plain synonym for essential or necessary.

entries.clue: English mutt spitting out one round date (5)

indicators.note: to spit something out is to expel it, as a dog drops a ball, so one O leaves the word

annotation.surface: An English dog spits out a round thing on a date.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Date' means a point in history, not a dinner out.
annotation.definitionFit: Epoch originally meant a fixed date from which time is reckoned, as astronomers still use it.

entries.clue: Greedy performer making a comeback (4)

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, and a return runs back the way it came, so read the word backwards

blocks.note: a diva is a star singer

annotation.surface: A greedy star stages a comeback tour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's comeback tour is exactly what a diva does, which hides the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Avid comes from Latin avidus, greedy, and keeps that sense in 'avid for money'.

entries.clue: Female group putting green car into empty bay (4)

indicators.note: putting means placing, which tells us to move the car somewhere
into gives the destination, the inside of the bay
an emptied word has its contents removed, leaving just the outer letters

blocks.note: an EV, electric vehicle, is a green car

annotation.surface: Some women park an electric car in an empty bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests colour; it means environmentally friendly.
annotation.definitionFit: Bevy is the traditional collective noun for ladies, as in a bevy of beauties.

entries.clue: Zeus’s daughter joining Demeter at Olympus (5)

indicators.note: the answer lies where the words join, spanning the gaps between them

annotation.surface: A daughter of Zeus joins the goddess Demeter on Mount Olympus.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is entirely Greek myth, and the answer belongs in that scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Erato, muse of love poetry, is one of the nine Muses, all daughters of Zeus.

entries.clue: Fired items in stock to cover different area (9)

indicators.note: held in, which places the new area inside the stock
a cover goes around what it protects, so the stock wraps the other letters

annotation.surface: Sacked staff are held in stock to cover a different region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fired' reads as sacked; it means baked in a kiln.
annotation.definitionFit: Stoneware is dense pottery baked in a kiln at high heat, so its pieces are fired items.

entries.clue: Capital tense with what was published (6)

blocks.note: T is short for tense in grammar
a story ran = it was printed

annotation.surface: A capital city is on edge about what has been published.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective, nervous; it gives the grammar abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

entries.clue: One in article really taking things wrongly (8)

indicators.note: one placed in the article sits inside it

annotation.surface: Someone in a newspaper article really misreads things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking things wrongly' suggests misunderstanding; it means stealing.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a cryptic paraphrase: thievery is taking what belongs to others, taking it wrongfully.
